The '''Geonosis droid factories''', also called the '''Geonosis droid foundries''', were massive subterranean [[Droid/Legends|droid]] factories, located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].<ref name="ITW:AOTC" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:ITW2_Droid_Factory.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Stalgasin hive/Legends|Stalgasin hive]] droid factory cutaway.]]
[[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] was ideal as a base for [[Droid/Legends|droid]] foundries in many regards: it was home to a technologically advanced but independent [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]], who could monitor and aid in droid production; its rugged, forbidding terrain more or less isolated it from outsiders, and its large underground caverns provided excellent camouflage against prying [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. Another prime benefit of locating the foundries on Geonosis was the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Mineral/Legends|mineral]]-rich ring system, used to provide the factories with ample raw metal and alloys.<ref name="ITW:AOTC" />

Like most other [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]] production facilities, the foundries on Geonosis were highly automated, requiring some [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] oversight and a steady flow of raw materials but little else. Despite being slow and antiquated by [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] standards, each facility boasted hundreds of conveyor belts and robot assembly arms, capable of creating thousands of droids per day from scratch. Due to its low-profile and remote location, the foundries kept a low standard on work safety, and expendable Geonosian drones were quartered in storage alcoves adjacent to the factory floors.<ref name="ITW:AOTC" />

Some of the main droid models produced by foundries on Geonosis included [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]], [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]], and powerful [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]]. In addition to droids, the factories produced vehicles, weapons and military parts.<ref name="ITW:AOTC" />

==History==
[[File:Droid_foundry.jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] being assembled]]

The foundries were built by [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]], a member of the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], in response to increasing legislation by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] against the legality of their industry, many centuries prior to the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]. Hoping to circumvent these new laws, BAW began investing in production facilities outside the Republic's sphere of influence: more specifically, in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], on planets such as [[Hypori/Legends|Hypori]], [[Olanet]], and [[Zaadja/Legends|Zaadja]].<ref name="DBGDF">{{DB|location|geonosisfoundry|Geonosis droid factory}}</ref>

The Republic encouraged the growth of such local industry as part of an idealist push for galactic cohesion and the spread of technology to the farthest corners of the galaxy. Eventually, this kind of political initiative disappeared, and the factories were abandoned. At some point before the start of the Clone Wars, they were reopened to supply the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] with droids, and were regarded by the Federation as its favorite weaponsmiths.<ref name="ITW:AOTC" />

During their mission to save [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], and the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] stumbled into one of the Geonosian droid assembly plants. Despite a brave effort, both Anakin and Padmé were apprehended and sentenced to death in the [[Petranaki arena]].<ref name="AOTC" />
In the ensuing [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], the [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] unit [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] was assigned to destroy a foundry and eliminate [[Sun Fac/Legends|Sun Fac]], [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser's]] chief lieutenant, which they successfully did.<ref name="RC">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref> After the Republic victory on that world, a garrison of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] was left behind to guard the planet.<ref name="I79">{{InsiderCite|79|Death in the Catacombs}}</ref>

Despite the Republic's victory, Poggle later built more factories on Geonosis, which were funded by the Trade Federation. Once the Jedi discovered this, they led a successful planet-wide invasion with the objectives of destroying the factories, capturing Poggle, and reclaiming the planet.

After the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|massacre]] of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]], Baktoid downsized and moved to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], reopening its factory on Geonosis, which had held out until the [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Confederacy's]] [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|end]].

==Behind the scenes==
The droid factory was a late addition in production, conceived and written into the story well after principal photography had wrapped. In the original shooting script, Anakin and Padmé crept into the Geonosian spire, and simply encountered Count Dooku. In this version, the droids R2-D2 and C-3PO never left the Naboo starship. The addition of the droid factory not only provided a new action set piece, but also gave a visual clue as to the size of the growing droid army. Elements of Anakin, Padmé and the droids were shot during additional photography in [[2001]], mostly against bluescreen with very minimal sets. The Animatics Department filled in the bluescreen areas with very detailed temporary versions of the droid factory, previsualizing the environment that [[Industrial Light & Magic]] would generate.

[[Ben Snow]], one the film's Visual Effects Supervisors, took reference footage of a Northern California automobile factory and foundry, to get visual starting points for the motion of automated machinery and the extreme heat and steam atmospheric effects his crew would recreate.

Though much of the environment was computer-generated, certain machines and the surrounding walls of the droid factory were realized as detailed and dramatically lit miniatures.<ref name="DBGDF" />
